title: SOLID Principles
readme:
# Day 18 — SOLID Principles

## Why This Day Matters

SOLID is not a set of rules — it's a set of **design forces**. Code that violates SOLID is harder to test, extend, and reason about. Code that follows SOLID tends to have small, cohesive units with minimal coupling.

## The Five Principles

| Letter | Name | One-liner |
|--------|------|----------|
| **S** | Single Responsibility | A class has one reason to change |
| **O** | Open/Closed | Open for extension, closed for modification |
| **L** | Liskov Substitution | Subtypes must be substitutable for base types |
| **I** | Interface Segregation | Many specific interfaces > one fat interface |
| **D** | Dependency Inversion | Depend on abstractions, not concretions |

## Learning Outcomes

- Identify SOLID violations in real code
- Apply each principle with a concrete C++ example
- Understand that over-engineering is also a problem (YAGNI)
- Know when to break the rules pragmatically

## Key Topics

- SRP: Cohesion and the "one reason to change" test
- OCP: Abstract base classes, virtual dispatch, `std::function` hooks
- LSP: Behavioral contracts, `noexcept`, invariant preservation
- ISP: Role interfaces, separating read from write, thin virtual bases
- DIP: Constructor injection, factory functions, mock-friendly design
